issues.legal_issue: A landlord may obtain eviction for a family member’s business conducted through a partnership with non-family members when the family member actively participates in the business and is not excluded from its management.
material_facts: The landlord sought the premises for his sons’ leather business, and the finding of bona fide need was not challenged.
The sons had previously participated actively in their father’s leather business and later became partners with others, jointly holding half the shares.
The partnership deed was silent about the sons’ roles, and there was no evidence that they were sleeping partners.
issues.conclusion: The sons’ active partnership business qualified as their business for the statutory eviction ground; the eviction order was upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(3)(a)(iii) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, a landlord may obtain eviction where the premises are needed for the business of the landlord or a qualifying family member. A partnership is a compendious description of the persons who constitute the firm under section 4 of the Partnership Act. A family member’s active participation in the partnership business can make it that family member’s business; but if the partnership deed expressly or impliedly excludes the family member from management and makes that person a sleeping partner, the premises are not needed directly or substantially for that person’s business occupation. The Court applied D.N. Sanghavi & Sons v. Ambalal Tribhuvan Das, [1974] 3 SCR 55, and distinguished Shantilal Thamordas v. Chimanlal Maganlal Telware, [1977] 1 SCR 341, which did not directly decide the question.

rule.if: commercial_eviction_proceeding and genuine_business_need_found and family_members_are_active_partners and not partnership_excludes_family_members_from_management

predicates.commercial_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant so that premises could be used for a family member’s business.
predicates.genuine_business_need_found: The courts found that the landlord genuinely needed the premises for the business, and that finding was not challenged.
predicates.family_members_are_active_partners: The landlord’s family members had participated in the business and were active partners in the partnership conducting it.
predicates.partnership_excludes_family_members_from: The partnership arrangement expressly or impliedly excluded the family members from management and made them sleeping partners.
predicates.eviction_order_upheld_for_family_busines: The eviction order is upheld because the premises are needed for the family members’ business.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks business-use eviction, a genuine need and active family-member participation in the partnership support upholding eviction, unless the partnership excludes those family members from management.
